stemMd: Two similar solids have corresponding lengths in the ratio $2:5$. The smaller solid has volume 48 cubic units. What is the larger volume?
explanationMd: Volumes of similar solids scale by the cube of the linear factor. The larger volume is 48(5/2)³=48(125/8)=6(125)=750.

distractorRationale.a: This scales volume by the linear factor only.
distractorRationale.b: This scales by the square, appropriate to area rather than volume.
distractorRationale.c: This does not apply the cube of 5/2 correctly.
